_doc: JOBEY dating cabinet (#42, Wave E, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #49). The murkiest American brand — pipedia itself: 'solid information is scant'. Probably ALWAYS American (Jobey brothers, Brooklyn, patent 1915; the England-origin lore unsupported). Spine = the distributor/owner ladder + two good cliffs: the JOBEY LINK stem (patent 1969/1970) and JOBEY DANSK (Karl Erik-made, 1970s-1987). SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Jobey.json (incl. the Tobacco World 1941 Norwalk find) + Weber_Pipe_Co_.json + Karl_Erik.json (cross-corroboration on Dansk + the 1987 Butz-Choquin transfer).

history_anchors._doc: 1915: brothers Ulysses + Louis Jobey (Brooklyn) patent a cavalier-style pipe (USD46998). 1918 Louis bankrupt; 1922 Ulysses Jr = VP of Lakewood Pipe Co (NJ). 1941: Tobacco World — NORWALK PIPE CORP, 'manufacturers of Jobey and Shellmoor pipes', president LOUIS JOBEY, moves to 218 E 26th St NYC. Distributor/owner ladder: George Yale Pipes & Tobacco NY (1942) -> Norwalk (1949) -> Arlington Briar Pipes, Brooklyn (undated) -> HOLLCO International (1969; the JOBEY LINK screw-tenon patent 1969/1970) -> WEBER PIPE CO, Jersey City (1970s, owner+maker) -> Tinder Box retail era (1970s-80s). JOBEY DANSK = Danish freehands bought from KARL ERIK OTTENDAHL (1970s; ended 1987 when KE stopped US exports). 1987: Jobey transferred as a ghost brand to BUTZ-CHOQUIN, Saint-Claude. Production later abandoned; 2002 F&K Cigar Co (St. Louis) re-introduces the brand. Mainly US/Canada/England markets; classic shapes, low-mid price ('a well made pipe for the price'; the '100-year briar, 1-in-500 bowls' ad copy = marketing).

brand_marks.physical: Classic-pattern pipes; the JOBEY LINK = screw-in tenon system (1969/70 patent) — its presence floors a pipe at 1969. Dansk pipes = Danish freehand style, KE workmanship (2SM-class stamps seen). Lines: Shellmoor (back to 1941!), Asti, Fawn Extra, Filtersan, Pinch, Unicorn, Specimen Grain, Air Cooled, Hand Rubbed.
